texts: Mannitol is the book's answer as the agent shown beneficial in several trials of spinal cord protection: A.
Mannitol, the many towels, is an osmotic agent that draws water out of swollen tissue and mops up free radicals, so it limits swelling of the ischaemic cord; it also protects the kidneys.
Nitroglycerin, the nitro dynamite, diazoxide and PARP inhibitors have not shown such benefit in patients; naloxone has some support, mostly together with spinal fluid drainage.
Memory hook: many towels soak the swollen cable dry.
